components.note: 非 (two things back-to-back) — 靠 relates to leaning against or relying on something
告 (gào) gives a sound distantly related to 靠's reading kào, having drifted apart over time
辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 近's meaning 'near, close,' a short distance to walk.
斤 (jīn) gives a sound hint — 近 is pronounced jìn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
刂 (a knife) — 刻 relates to carving with a blade
亥 (hài) is the historical phonetic element; it no longer closely matches 刻's modern reading kè
见 (to see) — 规 originally named a craftsman's compass, a tool used to observe and measure circles, extended to 'rule, regulation.'
夫 (fū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from guī.
贝 (a shell, an ancient form of currency/valuables) — represents the property or standards that rules protect.
刂 (a knife) — depicts laws being carved or inscribed onto a slate, the source of 则's meaning 'rule, standard.'
扌 (hand) — 接 relates to receiving or connecting something by hand.

至 (zhì, to arrive) — carries 到's core meaning, 'to reach, to arrive'

寸 (a hand) — a hand handing something over
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
阝 (a mound or place) — 队 pictures people gathering together.
人 (person) — people gathering in one place gave 队 its meaning 'a team' or 'a line/queue.'
贝 (shell/money — cowrie shells were historically used as currency) — 员 originally related to counting or officials responsible for accounts, later broadening to mean 'member' or 'personnel.'
Cloth/towel — hats are made of cloth.
Gives the sound mào, matching the character's reading.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.
办 (to manage/handle) — 协 relates to people working together to manage something
十 (shí) gives a sound distantly related to 协's reading xié, having drifted apart over time
讠 (speech) — relates to 议's meaning 'to discuss, deliberate; opinion.'

卩 (a person) — the one being dressed.
月 (a garment shape) — a hand 又 placing a coat on the person, giving 服 its meaning 'clothes; to obey, submit.'
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
冂 depicts a boundary or border enclosing an area.
土 (earth/land) — the land enclosed within the border.
口 here depicts a well within that land — together giving 周 its early meaning of a bounded territory, and later 'circumference, week, the Zhou dynasty.'
司 depicts a person with a raised arm giving orders — an official directing others, giving rise to the meaning 'to manage' or 'to take charge of.'
木 (wood) — 机 originally referred to a wooden device or machine, such as a loom.
几 depicts a small table or stool — combined with 木 (wood), the character pictured a wooden machine or mechanism.

叟 (sǒu) gives a sound close to sōu, differing mainly in tone.

屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.
日 (sun/day) — relates to 时's meaning of 'time, season'; the phonetic part of the character was later replaced by 寸 in the simplified form

弋 (a stake used to mark or catch something) — combined with 亻 (person), 代 came to mean a 'generation' or 'era,' and 'to take the place of' someone.

妾 (qiè) gives a hint of the sound — 接 is pronounced jiē, a connection that has shifted over time.

扌 (hand) — 抢 describes seizing or grabbing something forcefully.
仓 (cāng) is only distantly related in sound to qiǎng — both end in the -ang family, but the initial and tone have drifted apart.
Strength — force is used to take something.
Gives the sound qù, related to jié but drifted apart over time.
石 (rock) — 碰 originally described one hard object, like a stone, striking another, giving 'to bump, to collide.'

见 (to see) — 规 originally named a craftsman's compass, a tool used to observe and measure circles, extended to 'rule, regulation.'

矢 (arrow) — arrows were historically used as a measuring standard, tied to 矩's meaning 'a carpenter's square, a rule.'

A stylized foot (related to 止, 'to stop/foot') — originally meant 'to go,' later grammaticalized into a literary possessive/linking particle, similar to 的.
A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'
A pictograph of rising flames — the source of 火's meaning 'fire.'

讠 (speech) — 话 relates to speaking and words.
舌 (tongue) — the organ used for speaking, reinforcing 话's meaning of 'speech' or 'words.'
辶 (to walk) — 逃 means to escape or flee, involving movement.
兆 (zhào) gives a rhyme close to táo, with the initial shifted.
足 (foot) — 跑 describes an action done with the feet, running.
包 (bāo) gives a sound close to pǎo, sharing the same rhyme.
阝 (a variant of 邑, meaning place/settlement) — 部 relates to a division, section, or department.
咅 supplies the sound for 部 (bù); it belongs to the same phonetic family as related characters like 倍 (bèi) and 培 (péi).
门 is a picture of a double-leafed door or gate, drawn symmetrically to show two swinging panels.
土 (earth) — 基 relates to the ground or foundation something is built on.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 基 is pronounced jī, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
木 (tree) — provides the base image of a tree.
一 (a line) marks the base of the trunk, highlighting the roots — giving 本 its meaning 'root, origin, source.'
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
禾 (grain) — 租 originally described tribute paid in grain.
且 here marks the payment as regular and ongoing — combined with the grain 禾, it gave 租 its meaning 'rent, tax.'
A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'
八 (to divide/split apart) — represents something already split into parts.
刀 (knife) — a knife cutting already-divided pieces further, giving 分 its meaning 'to divide, to separate.'
木 (wood) — the thing being split apart.
斤 pictures an axe, the tool used to chop the wood, giving 析 its meaning 'to split, to analyze.'
亻 (person) — 代 relates to a person's place in time.
弋 (a stake used to mark or catch something) — combined with 亻 (person), 代 came to mean a 'generation' or 'era,' and 'to take the place of' someone.
介 (jiè) gives a sound hint — 价 is pronounced jià, sharing the same initial consonant though the vowel has shifted.
土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'
匸 (an enclosure or boundary) — 区 pictures a defined territory.
乂 (a mark, here representing control or division) — dividing land into bounded territories gave 区 its meaning 'district' or 'area.'
⺼ (flesh/body) — 背 refers to the back, a part of the body
北 (běi) gives a sound close to 背's reading bèi, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
Opposite/contrary — rebellion means going against something.
Gives the sound bàn, related to pàn but drifted apart over time.
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a human being.
一 (a line, here representing the sky) — drawn above a person, showing what is above them: the heavens, hence 'sky, day.'
土 (earth) — 堂 names a hall, a large room built on the ground.
尚 (shàng) gives a rhyme close to táng, with the initial shifted.
扌 (hand) — 拍 describes striking something lightly with the hand.
白 (bái) gives a sound distantly related to pāi, having drifted apart over time.
扌 (hand) — 摄 describes taking hold of or capturing something, as in taking a photograph.
聂 (niè) gives a sound distantly related to shè's reading, having drifted apart over time.
干 (originally a person) shown carrying a heavy load of grain on their back — since harvests came once a year, the character came to mean 'year.'
车 (cart) — 轻 originally described a light, nimble cart, extended to 'light (weight), gentle.'
工 (gōng) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from qīng.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
寸 (a hand) — guiding the way.

彳 (a road/step) — someone arriving on the road
寺 (a court/hall) — the destination where the visitor is welcomed
丶 (a dot) — represents the burning flame atop a lamp.

A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
釆 (to distinguish/sort) — 释 relates to sorting out and clarifying, i.e. 'to explain'
睪 (yì) gives a sound distantly related to 释's reading shì, having drifted apart over time
攵 (a hand with an implement, action) — relates to 放's meaning 'to let go, release, put.'

A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
行 (to go/walk) — 街 names a road where people walk and travel.
圭 (guī) gives a sound distantly related to jiē, having drifted apart over time.
⺮ (bamboo) — 箱 originally described a bamboo case or chest.
相 (xiāng) gives the sound — an exact match with 箱.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.
耳 (ear) — the original meaning of 耶 is unrelated to its modern use, which is mainly phonetic.
阝 (a place-name element) gives a sound distantly related to yé, having drifted apart over time.
禾 (grain) — 稣 was originally tied to reviving or gathering grain.
鱼 (yú) gives a sound only distantly related to sū today, having drifted apart over time.

巾 (cloth) — held in a hand, the image behind 布's meaning 'cloth' and, by extension, 'to spread out, distribute.'
扌 (hand) — a hand gripping something tightly
丸 (a pebble/pellet) — the small object held firmly in the hand
彳 depicts a step with the left foot; together with 亍 (a step with the right foot), 行 shows a person walking or moving.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 报 relates to taking action against someone.
卩 (a kneeling or bound person) — handling a wrongdoer and announcing the judgment gave 报 its meaning 'to report' or 'to announce.'
言 (speech) — 警 relates to speaking out a warning or alarm
敬 (jìng) gives a sound close to 警's reading jǐng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
又 (hand) and 寸 (also derived from a hand shape) — together suggesting two hands matching or corresponding, related to 对's meaning 'correct, matching.'
宓 depicts stillness and quiet beneath a roof.
山 (mountain) — a quiet, secluded mountain gave 密 its meaning 'dense, secret, close.'
石 (stone) — 码 originally related to counting stones used for reckoning, extended to mean 'number, code.'
马 (mǎ) is an exact match for the sound of 码.
纟 (silk/thread) — 红 originally described a color of dyed silk, hence 'red'
工 (gōng) gives a loose sound connection to 红's reading hóng
⺈ (a person, bent over) — the figure whose outward expression is being depicted.
巴 — traditionally linked to desire or emotion, so together the character points to a person's expression or complexion, extended to 色's meaning 'color, appearance.'
马 (horse) — 骗 originally described swinging up onto a horse, later extended figuratively to 'to trick, to swindle.'
扁 (biǎn) shares the rhyme -ian with piàn, and both use a bilabial initial (b/p) — only voicing and tone differ.
